entries.finding: check 1: hint 1 gives the definition of sovereignty
entries.reason: Hint 1 'a state's supreme power over its own territory, with no outside body above it' is the solution's definition of the answer, so it hands over D before any thinking. Codex's proposed wording repeated hint 2's 'not a relationship between states', so a shorter orienting hint was written instead.
entries.change: hint1 now points to the stem's key phrases ('govern itself', 'territorial integrity', 'without external intervention') and asks which basic concept they describe.

entries.finding: check 2: hint 3 restates option A
entries.reason: Once hint 2 has set aside the partisan option and hint 3 the garbled one, 'connects the media to government being answerable to citizens' paraphrases A, so no choice is left. Codex's fix repeated hint 2's partisan point, so it was reworded.
entries.change: hint3 now narrows to two and asks whose side each option puts the media on: a group seeking power, or the citizens who judge those in power.

entries.finding: check 2: hint 2 eliminates all three distractors
entries.reason: 'reduces competition or silences opposition' rules out A, C and D together, so hint 2 gives away B indirectly.
entries.change: hint2 replaced with Codex's wording, which rules out only the option about silencing opposition. hint3 unchanged.

entries.finding: check 2: hint 3 echoes the stem's 'potential'
entries.reason: 'building its ability to perform ... Which one makes the most of its potential?' can be matched to the stem's wording without any subject knowledge. Codex's fix used 'outdated', which points straight at retooling, so it was reworded.
entries.change: hint3 now names the two remaining options neutrally and asks which would fix a railway held back by worn-out engines and old methods.

entries.finding: check 2: hint 3 paraphrases 'by experts'
entries.reason: Hint 3 correctly narrows to two. The student still has to judge whether 'eliminates' makes C an overstatement, and that judgement is the skill being tested. Codex's replacement lists 'time' as a textbook reason, which would make C look correct.

entries.finding: check 2: hint 3 labels answer 'governance'
entries.reason: Labelling one option 'about people's confidence in government' and asking for 'a contribution to governance rather than to culture' can be answered from the labels alone. Codex's fix described option B as mobilising and dispute settling, which is not what B says, so it was reworded.
entries.change: hint3 now gives a concrete example (a chief persuading villagers to join an immunisation drive or register to vote) and asks which of the two options that kind of work fits.

entries.finding: check 10: 'assent' is a hard word
entries.reason: 'Approval' is plainer and means the same thing here, and the change is only in a distractor line.
entries.change: Why not the others D: 'needed his assent' changed to 'needed his approval'.

entries.finding: check 2: hints 2 and 3 together leave only B
entries.reason: Hint 2 removes A, then hint 3 removes both C and D and points to 'the one remaining', so no choice is left. Codex's fix spoke of 'the two remaining' when three were still in play, so it was reworded.
entries.change: hint3 now sets aside only C and asks which of the two options still in play weighs a strength against a weakness.

entries.finding: checks 8/11: 'cannot pursue trade, culture or anything else'
entries.reason: This is an unscoped absolute: insecure states still trade and hold cultural exchanges.
entries.change: 'cannot pursue' changed to 'struggles to pursue'.

entries.finding: check 2: hint 3 repeats hint 1's whole-vs-one-arm framing
entries.reason: 'One is about a single arm ... The other is about government as a whole. Which would make the whole state predictable?' answers itself after hint 1. Codex's reasoning-step idea was kept in a shorter form.
entries.change: hint3 now asks whether a state would be predictable if only the courts followed fixed rules while the President and the lawmakers did not.

entries.finding: check 2: hint 3 labels B 'the benefit its supporters promise'
entries.reason: Labelling one option as the supporters' promised benefit answers the stem's 'advocate' without any thinking. Codex's fix ('run a corporation better ... which option names that outcome') was still a direct match, so it was reworded.
entries.change: hint3 now asks the student to work out what 'redundancy' means for workers, then decide which option supporters would give as a reason.

entries.finding: check 2: hint 3 is a lopsided binary
entries.reason: 'how different they are, or ... a shared purpose written into the treaty' gives the answer away, since only one option is a purpose. Codex's timing idea was kept in a shorter form.
entries.change: hint3 now asks, for each remaining option, whether it was already true before 1975 or was something the members agreed to build together by signing the treaty.

entries.finding: check 11: 'is not their role' absolute beside 'mainly'
entries.reason: Some civil society groups do use civil disobedience, so a flat 'is not their role' overstates the case.
entries.change: Why not the others B replaced with Codex's scoped wording: they work mainly through lawful means such as advocacy and peaceful protest, not by deliberately breaking the law.

entries.finding: 'In a democracy the constitution is the highest law' stated as universal
entries.reason: Some democracies, such as the United Kingdom under parliamentary sovereignty, do not have a supreme written constitution, so this syllabus simplification needs a scope.
entries.change: Changed to 'In most democracies the constitution is the highest law.'

entries.finding: sibling leaks
entries.reason: No item in this paper has a passage_id or diagram, so there are no sibling groups and no hint can give away a sibling's answer.

entries.finding: hint 2 restates option A ('linked to accountability: making leaders answer to the people')
entries.reason: Hint 2 echoes the wording of option A almost word for word, so it states the answer indirectly, which hint 2 must not do.
entries.change: Hint 2 now contrasts a role serving all citizens with one serving a group, keeping the partisan elimination of D.

entries.finding: absolute 'a media that serves one party cannot hold the whole government to account'
entries.reason: Check 11: partisan outlets can still scrutinise a government, so 'cannot' is an unscoped absolute.
entries.change: D line now says it is partisan work for a party, not the media's general role of informing all citizens and checking those in power.

entries.finding: 'job cuts reduce capacity rather than build it' is unscoped
entries.reason: Check 11: cutting surplus staff does not always reduce capacity; the sound reason is that cuts alone do not fix the weaknesses named in the solution.
entries.change: C line: 'job cuts on their own do not fix old equipment or outdated methods'.

entries.finding: hint 3 lets the student pick B by sentence shape ('which one weighs a strength against a weakness')
entries.reason: Check 2: with hint 1 already saying a critical judgement weighs good and bad, hint 3 made B selectable by form alone.
entries.change: Hint 3 now asks the student to test the two remaining options against the historical record (unity against colonial rule, minorities pushed aside).

entries.finding: ungrammatical 'limits power rather than exists to protect'
entries.reason: Check 10: the phrasing is awkward. Self-applied check 11 also applies: a constitution does set out and secure executive powers, so saying it does not exist to protect them overstates.
entries.change: Hint 2: 'sets out and limits the power of each arm... Protecting one arm's power is not its main purpose.' B line: 'sets out the executive's powers mainly to define and limit them, and this concerns one arm only.'

entries.finding: 'members are neighbours that share borders' is inaccurate
entries.reason: Check 8: not every member borders the others, and Cabo Verde is an island state.
entries.change: C line: 'members are states in the same region, many of them sharing borders, and isolation would keep states apart, not bind them.'

entries.finding: hint 3 'Which of the two helps citizens take part in it?' paraphrases option C
entries.reason: Check 2: the question paraphrases 'facilitating citizen engagement', so the student can answer without thinking.
entries.change: Hint 3 now asks which option describes the broad, everyday work of these groups rather than a tactic used only now and then.

entries.finding: B line 'work mainly through lawful means... not by deliberately breaking the law' too categorical
entries.reason: The claim is already scoped by 'mainly', so it does not say that no group ever uses civil disobedience. It passes check 11 at syllabus depth.

entries.finding: sibling leak check
entries.reason: None of the six items has a passage_id or shared stem, so there are no siblings to leak to.
